title: Only a free call may be retried: one billed-attempt rule for http and router

Today: 2 dispatches, 1 served row, so the first billed attempt is never booked. After: 1 dispatch, 1 failed row, and the request fails `failed` without a blind second call

lib/imaging/router.ts:223-233 + :251-266 - billedOnFailure says `timeout` is BILLED and `failed` is billed iff dispatched. So the router's rule is that these attempts cost money, and http.ts repeats them for free

No persisted shape changes and no wire contract changes: error kinds stay inside the existing taxonomy, and 503 moves from `failed` to `rate-limited`, both of which already exist.

body:
## Summary
One rule decides whether a failed vendor attempt cost money, and both the transport retry in http.ts and the router's meter read it. A retry is allowed only for a call the rule says was free.

## Description
The router has a careful, enumerated answer to 'did this failure cost money' (`billedOnFailure`: timeout billed, dispatched failure billed, 429 not). One layer down, http.ts answers a different question, 'is it worth another go', and repeats exactly the attempts the router calls billed: a 5xx after the vendor answered, and a timeout it has itself marked `dispatched`. The result is three dispatches under one hold, one row in the ledger, and a meter that under-reads by up to 3x during an incident, which is the shape budget.ts's header calls the worst one a meter can have. On Leonardo it also re-POSTs a generation start, and that can leave remote generations no cleanup knows about. The video adapter in the same directory already made the opposite call (`attempts: 1` on its start).

The move: `presumedBilled(err)` lives in errors.ts as the single authority. `billedOnFailure` in router.ts becomes a re-export so the probe suite keeps asserting the same predicate. requestJson takes `billable: true` on vendor work requests (google interactions POSTs, leonardo start), and for those it retries only failures the authority says are free: 429, 503-as-capacity (kindForStatus maps 503 to `rate-limited`) and connect failures, which are never dispatched. Idempotent GET polls and DELETE cleanup keep their ladder. The router is unchanged in what it books. It now books every billed dispatch, because there is only ever one per candidate.

## Flow
- errors.ts: add `presumedBilled(err)` and move the enumerated switch here with its comment block
- router.ts: `billedOnFailure = presumedBilled` (still exported)
- http.ts: add the `billable` option. In the retry branches, `if (billable && presumedBilled(err)) throw err`. kindForStatus maps 503 to `rate-limited`
- google.ts: `billable: true` on the generate, edit and recognize POSTs. leonardo.ts: `billable: true` on POST /generations
- probe: a fetch stub that counts dispatches per URL. Cases 1-8

## Expected impact
Ledger rows equal billed dispatches (today up to 1 in 3). The ceiling sees every dispatch it admits. The worst-case wall time of a google generate drops from about 541 s to 180 s, inside the route's 300 s maxDuration. Leonardo can no longer create a generation the cleanup never sees. The cost is a transient 500 that used to heal silently: it now surfaces as `failed` and the surface's own retry is one visible, metered call. That is the trade the router's own billing rule already chose.

## Evaluation
Claim: no vendor attempt the router presumes billed is ever repeated without a ledger row and a hold
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard acceptance cases pass (2 guards green)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - tests/golden-path/imaging-billed-attempts.probe.spec.ts (Node probe lane, fetch stubbed, dispatches counted per URL), then the full `npm test` (imaging-budget-holds case 5 must stay green unchanged)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten (fewer automatic vendor calls; no ceiling, price or route contract loosened)

title: A paid render outlives its request: keyed receipts that join and replay

file_classes.lib/imaging/receipts.ts: hand (new, server-only like the rest of lib/imaging)
file_classes.tests/golden-path/imaging-receipts.probe: hand (new probe; two new tracked files change the kit census, which is generated by pipeline/kit-census.mts AFTER the commit and owned by the coordinator)

acceptance: receipts: two concurrent generate calls with the same (scope, key, body) -> the vendor fetch is dispatched once, both callers get byte-identical images, spendRows() has exactly 1 served row, and heldUsd while in flight equals one $0.045 estimate, not two

same (scope, key, body) again within the TTL after success -> 0 new dispatches, 0 new spend rows, and the result is marked replayed (response header `x-imaging-receipt: replayed`; the provenance is the original one, unchanged)
same (scope, key) with a different body hash -> 409 with code `idempotency-conflict`, 0 dispatches, nothing reserved
same key under a different principal scope -> treated as unrelated: it dispatches again and never returns the other scope's images

an owner call that fails (`refused`, `over-budget` or `no-key`) -> every in-flight joiner receives the same error kind. Nothing is retained, so the same key afterwards dispatches again (a 402 can pass after the window rolls)
an injected clock past the TTL, or the byte cap exceeded -> the receipt is evicted (oldest first) and the next call dispatches. The total retained base64 never exceeds the cap

imagingClient.generateImage with a fetch stub that throws a TypeError once and then answers 200 -> exactly 2 POSTs carrying the SAME `idempotency-key` header and identical bodies, and the call resolves. Today it throws `offline` after 1 POST
[guard] a POST without an `idempotency-key` header -> behaviour identical to today: dispatched, booked, no receipt retained
premise: docs/concepts/moonshots-2026-10-05/critic-2026-10-07-m1-tails.md:405-417 - verified: no route under app/api reads req.signal, and /api/imaging/generate awaits generate() with no signal. After a reload 'the paid image is generated, billed and thrown away'
app/api/imaging/generate/route.ts:25-41 and app/api/imaging/edit/route.ts:11-24 - the response is the only place the paid result lives. Nothing retains it past the request

lib/imagingClient.ts:187-197 - `post` turns any transport failure into `ImagingRequestError('The studio could not be reached.', 'offline', 0)` with no retry and no way to reattach. The only recovery is a fresh call, which bills again

app/_phases/frames/useFrames.ts:455-461, app/_phases/frames/alternatives/useAlternatives.ts:167-173, app/_phases/frames/ads/useAdsFrames.ts:39-45, app/library/Playground.tsx:213 - four surfaces call generateImage directly, so a client-level change reaches all four without editing any of them
lib/imaging/router.ts:315 + lib/imaging/budget.ts:389-392 - every dispatch reserves a hold. Two identical concurrent calls hold and book twice
lib/principal.ts:154 - `principalRateKey(resolution)` already yields a per-person key (the rate limiter uses it at lib/apiAuth.ts:488), so a receipt scope needs no new identity code
app/api/imaging/generate/route.ts:23 - maxDuration 300 bounds how long a joiner may wait on an owner
rollback: Additive. Without the header the routes take the old path (guard case 8). Reverting the series removes receipts.ts and the header handling, and the client stops minting keys. No persisted data: receipts are in-memory with a TTL. Nothing outside this context is edited.
runner_up: Stage as a request field: draft/proof/final picks image_size per call, instead of the module-load GOOGLE_IMAGE_SIZE at lib/imaging/providers/google.ts:53 (resolution-as-stage-property). Held because the 0.5K and 2K rows in pricing.ts are unmeasured and would book unpriced.
registry: software-engineering/concurrency-guards#idempotency-by-design, #guard-key-design, #cache-value-not-handle, #single-flight-primitives · software-engineering/retry-backoff#error-classification-for-retry ('a timed-out write ... needs an idempotency story before it needs a ladder') · software-engineering/cost-metering#reversible-debit-and-settle
body:
## Summary
Every money call carries an idempotency key. The server keeps the paid result as a short-lived receipt keyed by (principal, key, body hash). A duplicate request joins the call in flight or replays the result instead of paying again.

## Description
The imaging seam is fire-and-forget at the wrong layer. The server always finishes a render it started and bills it, but the only copy of the pixels is the HTTP response. A dropped connection, a dev reload, laptop sleep or a proxy idle timeout during a 60-180 s render therefore leaves a paid image on the server that nobody can claim. The client reports 'offline', and the user's next click pays a second time. The m1-tails critic proved this for the poster, and that one kind got a turn (lib/turns/kinds/poster.ts). This card fixes it once, at the imaging seam, for every caller: frames plates, alternatives, ads takes and Playground.

`lib/imaging/receipts.ts` is a keyed single-flight with a value cache. The key is (scope, key) and the entry stores a body hash. A miss claims the entry and runs the router. A hit with a settled value replays it. A hit in flight joins it, with the wait bounded by maxDuration. A body mismatch is a 409. Failures are never retained, so the money semantics of a refusal or a 402 do not change. Retention is bounded by TTL (15 min) and by bytes (64 MB of base64, oldest first), and stays per-process. On a scaled-out deploy, a retry that lands on another instance misses and degrades to today's behaviour. That is a safe failure, and the file/GCS store the spend kernel uses is the stated next step. The client mints `crypto.randomUUID()` per logical call, sends it as `idempotency-key`, and retries once with the same key on a transport failure or a 502/504 without a JSON code. It also exposes an optional `key` so a surface can later persist one and reattach after a reload.

## Flow
- receipts.ts: `withReceipt({scope, key, bodyHash, now}, run)` returns `{value, replayed}`, plus `__resetReceipts()` for probes
- api.ts: `asIdempotencyKey(header)` (1-128 printable chars, else 400), `bodyHash(validatedRequest)` (sha256 over canonical JSON including reference bytes), and a 409 mapping in errorResponse
- generate and edit routes: after guardRequest, resolve the scope (principalRateKey ?? clientIp), wrap generate()/edit() in withReceipt when the header is present, and set `x-imaging-receipt: replayed|joined|fresh`
- imagingClient.ts: the key header and the single same-key retry
- probe: cases 1-8, routes driven directly with the dev fixture (as imaging-auth.probe does)

## Expected impact
A transport failure during a render no longer costs a second render. Accidental double-submits are deduplicated server-side (one hold, one row). A surface gains a primitive to reattach to a paid render after a reload without a per-kind turn. This is the frames/alternatives/ads equivalent of what the poster got from turns, at one seam.

## Evaluation
Claim: an identical keyed request never dispatches or books a second vendor call while its first result is held
Before: 0 of 7 non-guard acceptance cases pass (1 guard green)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - tests/golden-path/imaging-receipts.probe.spec.ts (Node probe lane, fetch stubbed, dispatches and spendRows counted), then the full `npm test` and `npm run typecheck`
Result: better
Gate: contract (an optional request header and a 409 code on the in-tree /api/imaging money routes; the verifier is the new probe; no other repo consumes these routes)
